Tyson Fury has blamed Anthony Joshua for the years of delay that kept their mega-fight from happening sooner, claiming the British-Nigerian made “any excuse to get out” of it before the two finally signed. The two Britons will settle their decade-long feud on December 11 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, in a fight for the WBA “super” title. Fury said on the Mr Verzace Podcast that the contrast with his other big fights was telling. “When this fight is always talked about, it is never clean-cut. It is never like, ‘It is definitely going to happen,’ like all the other fights I have had, where even people who were arch-rivals like me and Deontay Wilder had done them three fights, and me and Usyk had the double, and me and Chisora had a trilogy, and many others as well, even Wladimir Klitschko back in the day,” he said. “They are all easy to make because people actually want to fight. But when you do not really want to fight, you are being forced into it; you are trying to make any excuse to get out of it. Why is it so easy to make all them other fights, but this one has always been difficult, always?” Okolie predicts Joshua knockout win over Fury I’ll bring more than power to Fury fight – Joshua Joshua reveals Usyk advice for Fury clash The former two-time heavyweight world champion pointed to his talks with Wilder, who had $50m on the table in the late 2010s. Fury said Wilder and his team, including Al Haymon, were easy to deal with despite the two men not getting along. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. In 2021, the pair were on a collision course until an arbitration hearing in the United States ruled that Wilder was owed a third fight with Fury. Doubts returned in April. Joshua was watching at ringside when Fury beat Arslanbek Makhmudov, but he refused to commit to facing his rival. Days later, the two signed, although there was a long delay before official details were released. Joshua booked his place in the clash in July, when he recovered from two knockdowns to stop Kristian Prenga in the second round. Fury had also stopped Mariusz Wach in his own warm-up bout.
